title: 13 Quo alternatives: What they won’t tell you
summary: Looking at Quo alternatives? See why 13 competitors don’t measure up and why small businesses often stick with Quo.
body_markdown:
No single business is best for everyone, and we’re the first to admit it. Yes, Quo, formerly OpenPhone, is a great fit as the phone platform for many growing businesses. But some alternatives bring real strengths of their own. Think video conferencing, physical desk phone rentals, or local numbers outside the US and Canada.


If you don’t need those specific features, we’ll make the case that Quo is the best phone system for small and growing businesses. And thousands of companies have already made that switch.


Along the way, we’ll also clear up a few misconceptions about Quo that keep surfacing in other “alternatives” roundups. That way, you’re comparing based on what’s true, not what someone else got wrong.


##


How we tested the Quo alternatives


**


Plenty of “alternatives” roundups claim every tool on the list was personally tested. But they miss certain features or claim the provider doesn’t have them. Or they compare one tool’s monthly rate against another’s annual rate or land on a price that doesn’t match either. If these comparisons were from first-hand testing, that’s not a small thing to miss.


Here’s how we made sure ours holds up:


- **Pricing.** Verified against each provider’s current, published pricing page at the time of writing. We also used the same billing cadence.
- **Features.** Checked directly against each provider’s own product pages, support documentation, and free trials. We didn’t rely on how a competitor’s roundup describes them.
- **Integrations.** Counted straight from each provider’s own integrations directory, not estimated or pulled secondhand.
- **Ratings.** Pulled from G2 and Capterra at the time of writing, with the review count listed alongside the star rating. That way, a 4.8 from 15 reviews doesn’t carry the same weight as a 4.7 from 3,000.
- **Implementation and support.** Checked each provider’s onboarding process and support channel availability by plan tier. We also looked at number porting assistance and help documentation.
- **Hands-on testing.** For a handful of the tools on this list, we signed up directly, ported a number, and made and received real calls on the platform ourselves.


##


**Let’s set the record straight: 6 Misconceptions about Quo**


A lot of “Quo alternatives” roundups get basic facts about Quo wrong. Some mix up monthly and annual pricing so their tool appears to be more cost-effective. Others say Quo is missing features it already has.


So before you pick an alternative off someone else’s chart, get the real picture first.


Here’s what’s actually true… and what isn’t.


Claim Verdict The facts


Quo has no AI receptionist False Sona, Quo’s AI voice agent, is included on every plan. Every workspace gets 1,000 free credits per month, or about 10 Sona-handled calls. You can buy more credits based on your needs.


Quo’s CRM sync is limited False Quo natively syncs with HubSpot, Salesforce, Pipedrive, Zoho CRM, Attio, Jobber, JobTread, Housecall Pro, and Clio, with more being added consistently.


Quo’s AI features are an add-on Misleading Sona itself, along with call summaries and transcripts for Sona-handled calls, are included on every plan. Call summaries and transcripts are available from the Business plan, and AI call tags are available on the Scale plan. All standard, not add-ons. You only need to purchase more credits for more Sona calls beyond the free monthly allotment.


Quo doesn’t offer free migration help False Number porting is free. Quo’s team prepares the Letter of Authorization and coordinates with the old carrier.


Quo’s HIPAA restrictions on SMS are a shortfall unique to Quo Misleading SMS/MMS aren’t inherently HIPAA-compliant channels for any provider. This is an industry-wide constraint, not something specific to Quo.


Quo’s support is email-only Misleading True for the Starter plan. Business plan users also have access to live chat support. The Scale plan includes inbound phone support during business hours.


With the record straight, you can now compare Quo alternatives more fairly. Here are 13 options to consider.


##


**13 Best Quo alternatives compared**


Before we dive into the details, here’s how each virtual phone system stacks up:

### **1. Vonage: Best alternative with an API offering**


#### Pros


- Unlimited domestic calls in the US and Canada
- API add-ons for building a custom solution


#### Cons


- Call recording, voicemail transcripts, and toll-free numbers are paid add-ons
- No AI features like call summaries or message responses
- Pricing isn’t fully transparent, with extra fees for support, recording, and transcripts


[Vonage](https://www.quo.com/blog/vonage-alternatives/) offers unlimited domestic calling on Android, iOS, and desktop. There are also API add-ons that let developers build custom voice, SMS, and video features into their own apps.


While Vonage offers many of the features Quo has, most are paid add-ons. For example, you have to pay extra for toll-free numbers. And unless you upgrade to the most expensive Vonage plan, you also have to pay add-on fees for voicemail transcriptions and on-demand call recording.


That means the figure you see on Vonage’s pricing page isn’t necessarily what you’ll pay. For teams of up to four members, Vonage starts at $13.99 per number per month. But you also have to factor in extra fees for basic features that come standard on Quo plans.


#### Vonage pricing


**


As mentioned,[Vonage’s pricing](https://www.quo.com/blog/vonage-pricing/) depends on how many people are on your plan. If you sign up between one and four users, here’s how their plans break down:


- **Mobile:** $13.99 per number per month to access unlimited domestic calling, SMS and MMS,[virtual receptioni](https://www.quo.com/product/virtual-receptionist) st, and support for desktop and mobile apps
- **Premium:** $20.99 per number per month to access unlimited video meetings with up to 200 participants, integrations with business apps, analytics and reporting, and support for VoIP desk phones
- **Advanced:** $27.99 per number per month to access single sign-on, on-demand call recording, voicemail transcription, and call groups


You can get a full comparison of[Quo vs Vonage](https://www.quo.com/compare/quo-vs-vonage) .


### **2. RingCentral: Best alternative with desk phone rental options**


#### Pros


- Unlimited calls to the US and Canada
- Videoconferencing is available
- Desk phone rentals


#### Cons


- Only 25 texts per user per month on the base plan, with per-message overage charges
- Call recordings and files expire after 90 days
- Caps on toll-free minutes
- Desk phone rentals require multi-year contracts


[RingCentral](https://www.quo.com/blog/ringcentral-alternatives/) is an older business phone system that offers calling, texting, and video conferencing. It also works on smartphones, computers, and desk phones. This can be useful if you already own physical phone equipment and want to keep using it.


With RingCentral, you can get some of the features available in Quo, with significantly more limitations. The base plan only provides 100 toll-free minutes, 25 text messages, and limited storage. Even the most expensive plan only allows for 200 messages per user per month. Quo provides unlimited text messaging in the US and Canada with each plan, so you can scale your business without paying extra.


RingCentral users also report a less-than-ideal user experience. One[G2 reviewer](https://www.g2.com/products/ringcx/reviews/ringcx-review-13671011) notes: “The interface feels a little confusing to navigate, and I’ve also noticed occasional delays or minor glitches during calls.”


No matter how much you upgrade, you’re also subject to storage retention policies that delete most of your data. That includes[call recordings](https://www.quo.com/blog/ringcentral-recording-calls/) and[call logs](https://www.quo.com/product/call-analytics/call-logs) . Recordings and other files expire after 90 days, which makes it harder for teams with long sales cycles.


#### RingCentral pricing


**


There are four tiers of[RingCentral’s pricing](https://www.quo.com/blog/ringcentral-pricing/) :


- **Core:** $20 per user per month for unlimited domestic calling, 25 texts per user, and 100 pooled toll-free minutes
- **Advanced:** $25 per user per month for auto call recording, app integrations like Salesforce and Zendesk, 100 texts per user, and 1,000 pooled toll-free minutes
- **AI Customer Engagement Bundle with AIR** : Contact sales for pricing for 10,000 pooled toll-free minutes, 200 SMS per user, unlimited storage, and historical and real-time insights
- **AI Customer Engagement Bundle with AIR and ACE** : Contact sales for pricing for AI Conversation Expert (ACE), coaching and performance analytics, and CRM and productivity integrations


There’s also a Business SMS Booster and a Call Queues Booster add-on that gives you some features from the Customer Engagement Bundle. You’ll get shared inboxes, texts, compliance tools, and more for another $25 per month.


### **3. Dialpad: Best alternative for managing call centers**


#### Pros


- Unlimited calling in the US and Canada
- Live call transcription and real-time analytics
- Real-time AI-powered speech coaching
- Local number support in 50+ countries


#### Cons


- Toll-free numbers cost $15 per month
- Basic integrations like Slack and Zapier are locked behind upgrades
- User minimums on higher-tier plans


[Dialpad](https://www.quo.com/blog/dialpad-alternatives/) is a cloud phone system that includes video conferencing on every plan, along with AI coaching tools. Its base plan starts at $15 per user per month and includes basic phone features.


But Dialpad is bloated with features that may suit call centers more than fast-growing businesses. You may not need video calling or whiteboarding with Miro, but that’s what you get when you pay for a Dialpad plan. Some of Dialpad’s most basic features are locked behind more expensive plans. You can’t set up integrations or add numbers unless you pay for the Pro plan, which costs $25 per user per month.


You also only get 250 text messages per user per month with[Dialpad SMS](https://www.quo.com/blog/dialpad-sms/) . After that, you’ll pay $0.008 per outbound SMS and $0.024 per outbound MMS. Want to buy additional numbers? You’ll need the Pro plan at $25 per user per month. For more toll-free numbers, you’ll pay $15 or $17 per number, depending on whether you pay monthly or annually. You’ll also pay $0.02 per minute for incoming calls.


#### Dialpad pricing


**


There are three[Dialpad pricing plans](https://www.quo.com/blog/dialpad-pricing/) :


- **Standard** : $15 per user per month for Dialpad SMS, Google Workspace integrations, and AI-powered call and voicemail transcriptions
- **Pro** : $25 per user per month for international texting, CRM integrations, auto-replies, and the option to have additional numbers, with a three-user minimum
- **Enterprise** : Call for a quote to get SSO integrations, live agent support, 100% uptime, and unlimited locations and ring groups, with a 100-user minimum


### **4. **GoTo Connect: Best for Microsoft 365 users****


#### Pros


- Native Microsoft 365 integration
- Unlimited calling to 50+ countries on the Standard plan
- Drag-and-drop call flow builder


#### Cons


- Costly toll-free minutes capped at 1,000 per month, then billed per minute
- No public pricing, so you have to talk to sales for a quote
- SMS limits, depending on the plan
- Team inboxes require an upgrade


[GoTo Connect](https://www.quo.com/blog/goto-connect-alternatives/) is a cloud-based VoIP phone system. It integrates with platforms like Microsoft Teams and Outlook. This lets you call and text from inside the apps. You also get video meetings with GoTo Connect, even on its base plan.


That said, GoTo Connect’s pricing isn’t public. This might make it hard to decide whether it’s the right Quo alternative for your business.


But we do have *some* idea of the fees you’ll pay — including for SMS. You only get access to 80 SMS credits per user each month. After that, you’ll pay $0.0055 per message. But this cost can vary depending on where you live, like in the US versus the UK.


#### GoTo Connect pricing


**


GoTo Connect doesn’t currently list its pricing. The only way to get a quote is to contact sales.


### **5. Ooma: Best alternative with legacy features**


#### Pros


- Unlimited calls in the US, Canada, Mexico, and Puerto Rico
- Ring groups on the base plan
- Analog fax machine support


#### Cons


- Base plan doesn’t come with texting
- Limited toll-free minutes
- Call recording requires an upgrade


[Ooma](https://www.quo.com/blog/ooma-alternatives/) is a Quo alternative that sells its own line of[VoIP phones](https://www.quo.com/blog/what-is-a-voip-phone/) , including a few wireless options. They also have a[hosted PBX](https://www.quo.com/blog/hosted-pbx/) solution that connects to traditional hardware like fax machines and overhead pagers. It’s a good alternative if you’re looking to modernize legacy analog hardware.


Unfortunately, Ooma doesn’t offer texting on the base plan. Even with the most expensive plan, you’re limited to 1,000 messages sent and received per account per month.


What about CRM integrations? Or AI features like transcriptions or insights? You’ll have to upgrade twice. Just keep in mind some features still require add-ons after upgrading, like Ooma’s AI receptionist.


#### Ooma pricing


**


Here’s what to expect from[Ooma’s pricing plans](https://www.quo.com/blog/ooma-pricing/) :


- **Essentials:** $19.95 per user per month for auto-attendants, conference calling, call forwarding, and overhead paging support
- **Pro:** $24.95 per user per month for call recording, voicemail transcriptions, dynamic caller ID, video conferencing, analytics, SMS, and Ooma’s desktop app with calling features
- **Pro Plus:** $29.95 per user per month for call queuing, CRM integrations, hot desking, shared voicemail boxes, and advanced call flows
- **Enterprise:** Custom pricing for SIP trunking, Microsoft Teams integration, advanced analytics, and direct team routing


For additional numbers, you’ll pay $9.95 per number per month.


### **6. Nextiva: Best Quo alternative for omnichannel communication**


#### Pros


- Video calling available on the base plan
- Social media channel management
- Routes voice, chat, SMS, and social channels like WhatsApp into one inbox


#### Cons


- SMS is capped at 100 messages per user per month on the base plan
- Call recording requires an upgrade
- Toll-free numbers and minutes require an upgrade


[Nextiva](https://www.quo.com/blog/nextiva-alternatives/) is a Quo alternative focused on omnichannel communication. It helps you handle customer conversations by phone and text. You can also chat, video call, and message customers via apps like WhatsApp and Microsoft Teams.


But Nextiva plans aren’t friendly to small businesses:


- Nextiva only offers integrations with CRMs like Salesforce and HubSpot as an additional add-on.
- SMS is limited to 100 messages sent and received per user per month before you’re charged extra.
- Nextiva offers toll-free numbers but doesn’t include toll-free minutes on the base plan. Even if you upgrade to the Engage plan, you’re limited to 2,000 toll-free minutes and 500 texts per user per month.


#### Nextiva pricing


**


Here’s what to expect from[Nextiva pricing plans](https://www.quo.com/blog/nextiva-pricing/) :


- **Core:** $15 per user per month for voice calls, up to 100 text messages per user, simple IVR, and voicemail transcriptions
- **Engage:** $25 per user per month for one toll-free number and 2,000 toll-free minutes, 500 text messages per user, Microsoft Teams integration, and video meeting recordings
- **Scale:** $75 per user per month for unlimited texting, up to 10,000 toll-free minutes, the inbound sales and service call center, priority and skills-based routing,[automatic call distribution](https://www.quo.com/product/call-routing/automatic-call-distribution) callback, and access to the supervisor dashboard


### ****7** . Allo: Best for mobile-first small teams**


#### Pros


- Cheap solo plan coming soon
- Supports 20+ countries and multiple languages
- AI receptionist


#### Cons


- Pricing jumps a lot between plans
- Base plan doesn’t support sending texts or a desktop app
- Base plan only keeps AI summaries and transcripts for 30 days


Allo is a newer phone system for sales teams. It’s not quite as established as some other competitors on this list. But it gives you one business number per user, unlimited national calls, and unlimited inbound SMS. Plans for teams also give you free outbound SMS to US numbers.


The solo plan includes AI call summaries and transcripts, stored for 30 days. Upgrade and you’ll get unlimited storage for transcripts and summaries, along with AI call tags and post-call actions. There’s also an AI search assistant that can pull up details about contacts or past conversations. While Allo has an AI receptionist, it’s an add-on that costs $32 per agent per month.


Pricing is affordable if you’re a single user. But once you have a team or want to send texts, the cost jumps significantly.


Another thing to know about Allo: past users say it’s not yet feature-rich. As a newer tool, it’s missing features and offering services that aren’t as advanced as competitors.


This reviewer provides firsthand knowledge:


“Yes, there are certain features that could be improved, like the dashboard. Some missing features, especially on the standard \[plan\], are still inferior to what we currently have…” —[G2](https://www.g2.com/products/the-mobile-first-company-allo/reviews/allo-review-12314842)


#### Allo pricing


**


You have three Allo pricing plans to choose from:


- **Solo** : $10 per month for one user, unlimited national calls, one number, call recording, AI call summaries and transcripts, and email support. At the time of writing, this plan isn’t publicly available yet.
- **Business** : $32 per user per month for unlimited users with one number each, CRM sync with call tags in HubSpot, Pipedrive, Attio, and Salesforce, SMS support, custom AI summary templates, AI post-call actions, call analytics, and MCP connectors with Claude and ChatGPT
- **Ultra** : $100 per user per month for AI agents like the AI SDR, AI CRM manager, and AI sales coach, custom analytics dashboards, a custom AI voice for IVR, Slack support, a dedicated account manager, and custom onboarding


The AI receptionist costs $32 per agent per month, or the price of a Business user seat, to answer inbound calls.


### **8. KrispCall: Best Quo alternative for outbound sales and cold calling**


#### Pros


- Virtual numbers for 100+ countries
- 100+ integrations are available from the base plan
- Bulk SMS campaigns and power dialer with an upgrade


#### Cons


- Call transfer requires an upgrade
- No call recording and storage on the base plan
- Limited SMS and calling on almost all plans


KrispCall is a cloud phone solution designed for outbound sales teams. It includes a power dialer and, with an add-on, international numbers in 100+ countries. Every plan comes with a free US, Canadian, or UK number per user and limited calling minutes and SMS segments. It also has integrations with 100+ CRMs and tools from the base plan. The only one that needs an upgrade is Salesforce.


As mentioned, calling and texting are capped on most tiers. Starter includes 200 inbound and 200 outbound minutes per user each month, and 100 SMS segments. Advance bumps that to 1,000 minutes each way and 1,000 SMS segments. Max removes the *calling* cap, but SMS stays capped at 1,000 segments per user.


While the base plan may seem affordable at $12 per user per month, you’ll pay separately for calls and texts. So KrispCall may not be the best Quo alternative for small and growing businesses that expect a predictable bill every month.


#### KrispCall pricing


**


KrispCall has four pricing plans to choose from:


- **Starter:** $12 per user per month for up to five users, one free local number per user, 200 inbound and 200 outbound call minutes, 100 SMS segments, and 100+ integrations
- **Advance:** $32 per user per month for up to 50 users, 1,000 inbound and 1,000 outbound call minutes, 1,000 SMS segments, call recording and transfer, power dialer, bulk SMS campaigns, and CRM integrations, including Salesforce
- **Max:** $48 per user per month for unlimited users, eligible unlimited inbound and outbound calling subject to fair-use limits, and 1,000 SMS segments per user
- **Enterprise:** Custom pricing for 50+ seats, with bundled calling and SMS rates, a dedicated account manager, and custom integrations


### **9. Grasshopper: Best alternative for multi-digit extensions**


#### Pros


- Unlimited calling to the US and Canada
- Auto-attendant phone menu with extensions
- Voicemail transcriptions


#### Cons


- Unlimited users require an upgrade
- No third-party integrations
- Limited productivity features
- Call recording requires an upgrade
- $500 deposit required for international calling; Hawaii and Alaska count as international locations


[Grasshopper](https://www.quo.com/blog/grasshopper-alternatives/) is an older virtual phone system built for solo operators and very small teams. Its biggest claim to fame is multi-digit extensions. You get one main number with extensions for individuals or departments, so you don’t need separate numbers for everyone on your team.


Most features are standard on every plan, so you don’t need to shop for the best tier. Unlike Quo, Grasshopper’s cost depends on how many phone numbers and extensions you want.


This isn’t necessarily cheaper. Grasshopper’s least expensive plan starts at $14 per month, but you have to upgrade if you want more than one user. Even then, you still get only one number per account unless you upgrade to the most expensive plan. Additional numbers cost $9 per number per month. That means you have to pay $34 per month for two users and two business numbers. With Quo, that same scenario would cost just $30 per month. Additional numbers on Quo cost $5 per number per month.


Even if you pay extra for Grasshopper, it may not have the features many growing teams want. All plans come with the same basics, like calling, texting, and voicemail. But you don’t get necessary features like CRM integrations or automated texting workflows beyond auto-replies.


#### Grasshopper pricing


**


[Grasshopper’s pricing plans](https://www.quo.com/blog/grasshopper-pricing/) for small businesses include:


- **True Solo:** $14 per month for one user, one phone number, and one extension
- **Solo Plus:** $25 per month for unlimited users, one phone number, and three extensions
- **Small Business:** $55 per month for unlimited users, four phone numbers, and unlimited extensions


### **10. MightyCall: Best alternative if you don’t need advanced SMS features**


#### Pros


- Unlimited call and text support in the US and Canada
- International numbers are available, with an upgrade
- HIPAA compliance for healthcare providers


#### Cons


- Limited CRM integrations
- Three-user minimum on plans


[MightyCall](https://www.quo.com/blog/mightycall-alternatives/) is an alternative to Quo, offering call management software for customer support teams. Each plan includes unlimited calls and texts in the US and Canada, as well as a mobile app and web phone support so you can take calls on the go.


Just know that there’s a three-user minimum on every plan. This means you’re not actually paying $20 per month for the base tier as advertised. Instead, the base plan cost starts at $60 per month. Other features involve extra steps. For example, you only get AI call summaries after upgrading your plan. Then you’ll need to submit a request through the sales or support team to access them.


Users have also reported connection issues:


*“There are times when we have connection issues, especially with transferring calls. However, uninstalling and reinstalling the app typically fixes that.”* —[G2](https://www.g2.com/products/mightycall/reviews/mightycall-review-11276984)


#### MightyCall pricing


**


[MightyCall offers four plans](https://www.quo.com/blog/mightycall-pricing/) to choose from:


- **Core:** $20 per user per month with a three-user minimum to access unlimited calling, unlimited messaging, and three business phone numbers
- **Pro:** $38 per user per month with a three-user minimum to unlock supervisor workspace, live call monitoring, and analytics and reporting
- **Power: $54 per user per month** to access Preview dialer, Progressive dialer, and a dedicated account manager
- **Enterprise:** $65 per user per month to access Predictive dialer, SIP trunking support, and custom integrations


### **11. Aircall: Best alternative for global call centers**


#### Pros


- Power Dialer makes calls in rapid succession
- Call routing and IVR menus on the base plan
- Can buy international numbers in more than 100 countries


#### Cons


- SMS and MMS aren’t unlimited
- User minimums on every plan
- AI call summaries require an add-on


[Aircall](https://www.quo.com/blog/aircall-alternatives/) is a business phone system for sales and support teams that handle high call volumes. Its power dialer helps outbound teams move through call lists faster. Features like call whispering and live coaching give managers more control over rep performance. Aircall also offers AI Assist as an add-on for AI coaching on calls.


Keep in mind that every plan has user limits. The Essentials plan requires at least three users, so the listed $30 per-user price is actually a $90 per-month minimum. Their highest-tier plan also requires at least 25 users. If you’re a team of one or two, you’ll pay for more seats than you need. Quo is designed for small and growing businesses, so you can simply add or remove users as needed.


Aircall also charges extra for analytics features like heatmaps and per-rep insights. Quo includes these features in our Business and Scale plans.


#### Aircall pricing


**


All[Aircall pricing](https://quo.com/blog/aircall-pricing) plans have user minimums. Essentials and Professional require three users, and Custom requires 25.


Here are the features you can expect on each tier:


- **Essentials:** $30 per user per month for unlimited Canadian and US calls, call routing, SMS and MMS support, 50 free AI agent minutes per account per month, and IVR support
- **Professional:** $50 per user per month for smart routing, queue callbacks, and access to the power dialer
- **Custom:** Custom pricing for unlimited global calling, custom onboarding, and service-level agreements


Aircall also has an AI Voice Agents plan, starting at $100 per month. This gives you an AI receptionist that can take calls, answer FAQs, and make outbound calls. However,their cost calculator shows the minimum is $175 a month for a bundle of 500 minutes. They have a pay-as-you-go option for $0.49 a minute. For specific costs, it’s best to discuss your monthly needs with Aircall’s sales team.


### **12. **Zoom Phone:** Best alternatives for Zoom Workplace users**


#### Pros


- Natively connected to Zoom Workplace video meetings
- Call recording is included on every plan
- Bundled discount pricing when paired with Zoom Workplace


#### Cons


- Unlimited domestic calling requires an upgrade from the base metered plan
- Third-party phone integrations are limited compared to fuller business phone systems
- Limits on shared phone numbers


Zoom Phone is the business phone companion to Zoom’s video conferencing platform. Beyond meetings, Zoom Phone offers calling, texting, and voicemail in the same app.


The base plan has an affordable starting price, but your calling is metered. SMS and MMS are also limited; you can’t text as a team without paying for the Customer Engagement Pack. That costs an extra $25 per user per month, which can be a significant drawback for scaling teams. Quo includes unlimited calling and texting in all of its plans.


Finally, you only get a few integrations with Zoom Phone, which can mean more manual work as your business grows:


- Salesforce
- Slack
- Microsoft Calendar and Outlook
- Google Calendar and Gmail
- Twilio
- [Five9](https://www.quo.com/blog/five9-alternatives/)
- Genesys
- NICE inContact
- Talkdesk


If you’re a growing small business looking to connect with CRMs like HubSpot, you might consider a[Zoom Phone alternative](https://www.quo.com/blog/zoom-phone-alternatives/) .


#### Zoom Phone pricing


**


[Zoom Phone’s pricing](https://www.quo.com/blog/zoom-phone-pricing/) includes five plans:


- **US & Canada Metered** : $10.50 per user per month for metered domestic calling, domestic SMS and MMS, 50 pages of online fax, and AI features like AI call summaries, voicemail prioritization, and AI Companion
- **US & Canada Unlimited** : $16 per user per month for all Metered features, plus unlimited domestic calling
- **Pro Plus** : $20.50 per user per month for video management tools, Workplace integrations like Microsoft and Salesforce, 15 GB cloud storage per user, unlimited AI meeting summaries, access to the agent builder, and eight custom AI meeting summary templates


- **Global Select** : $22 per user per month for unlimited domestic calling in 40+ countries and territories, one direct dial number per license, and unlimited online fax
- **Business Plus** : $24.50 per user per month for unlimited domestic calling, 300 meeting participants, device management, 15 GB cloud storage per user, unlimited AI notetaking, summaries, and queries


They offer two ways to get the AI receptionist add-on: a standalone plan starting at $25 per month for 100 minutes, billed annually, that works with any phone system, or an add-on rate for existing Zoom Phone users starting at $0.30 per minute, billed annually, plus the cost of your underlying plan.


### **13. Ringly: Best Quo alternative with a Shopify integration**


#### Pros


- AI agent can autonomously handle inbound ecommerce calls
- Native Shopify integration
- 40+ languages supported
- 14-day free trial for the Pro plan


#### Cons


- Smaller volume sellers might struggle to justify the price
